summary: Iteration 5 targeted re-test of the iteration_4 CRITICAL duplicate-stop bug (VRPTW optimize with no warehouse start) + full backend regression + quick frontend regression. RESULT: bug is FIXED. Backend: all 73 tests in /app/backend/tests/ pass (including test_vrptw_no_depot.py which previously failed by design). Frontend: import 36 stops -> untyped modal(5) -> 'Respetar horarios' ON + salida 08:00 -> Optimizar ruta returns 36 stops (KPI Paradas=36, 36 unique stop-item testids, 36 ETA badges, ZERO console errors / no React duplicate-key warnings). Drivers CRUD (add/list/delete) works via UI + API. Editable window inputs are now readable (12h value not clipped) and editing stop-wto-1 to 08:05 triggered GET /api/route 200 and updated the schedule bar from 'Todo en horario' to '1 fuera de horario'.

minor.issue: Carry-over from iteration_4 (unchanged, non-blocking): solve_vrptw skips window constraints for the start node, so when there is no warehouse the first stop's ventana horaria is silently ignored. Decide expected behaviour or warn the user.

issues: wh-departure and stop-wfrom/wto are still native browser time pickers (12h 'AM/PM' + native clock icon) inside the custom dark UI — values are now fully readable after the 96px widening, but the control style remains inconsistent with the design system (cosmetic, unchanged from iteration_4).

action_items: No blocking action items. Optionally address the ignored first-stop time window when no warehouse start is configured, and optionally replace native time inputs with a custom 24h control.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py optimize(): the VRPTW branch now dedupes stop_order with a seen-set (verified lines ~665-672) so both branches honour the same contract (unique ids, len == n_stops). Good.

App.js handleOptimize: `const uniqueOrder = [...new Set(data.order)]` is a solid defensive guard; note that stops dropped by the filter(Boolean) would silently shrink the list — consider logging a warning if uniqueOrder.length !== stops.length.

App.js handleImport does NOT call recalc(), so right after import Distancia/Tiempo show '—' and no schedule-bar until 'Optimizar ruta' is pressed. Intentional? (my initial test wrongly expected a route after import).

success_rate.frontend: 100% of retested flows (duplicate-stop fix, drivers CRUD, window edit recalc, schedule bar, ETA badges)

seed_data_creation: Created and deleted two temporary drivers (QAT1 Retest via UI+API DELETE, QAT2 Del via UI delete). No leftover test data. Settings currently: departure_time=null, respect_windows=true, service_by_type P=3/PD=4/L=6 (departure field renders empty on load — set it in the UI before optimizing with windows).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Duplicate-stop VRPTW bug is fixed and covered by tests/test_vrptw_no_depot.py. Full suite: 73 tests, 43s, run `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -v`. Frontend flow timings: import sample_stops.xlsx ~5s, VRPTW optimize over 36 stops ~10-15s (poll for [data-testid=schedule-bar]). Gotchas: wh-respect is a native checkbox -> use is_checked() (not data-state) and it is persisted as true, so a blind click turns it OFF; departure_time in settings is currently null so fill wh-departure with '08:00' before optimizing; drivers delete button must be located by its exact data-testid (delete-driver-{id}) — using .last was flaky once.
rca_of_the_issue: Fixed as recommended: server.py VRPTW branch builds stop_order via a seen_ids set so the closed-tour depot stop id is emitted only once; App.js also dedupes data.order. Verified end-to-end: 3-stop no-warehouse VRPTW returns unique order len==3, and 36-stop UI run renders exactly 36 stop items with no React duplicate-key errors.
